rows.selected_entry: Original EM public prepare/check entry and configuration SDK using selected installed command-execution dependency through unchanged facades
rows.observation_boundary: Reuse PKG-R06 original supported-operation compatibility observations plus PKG-R02–05 preserved semantics through actual facade/dependency import. Real isolated nonempty operation and real temporary configuration edit/read use selected candidate runtime.
rows.required_behavior: Original configuration/prepare/execute/interpreter operations preserve supported results/errors and complete streams.
rows.expected_result: Authored expected config state and unchanged metadata/order, independently expected argv/cwd/env, full child stdout/stderr/exit, correct configured nonzero success and failed-command stopping. Original consumer operation reports correct success/failure with actual attempted commands.
rows.oracle: Accepted AS-IS source contracts and actual four original characterizations, maintained original-owner supported-operation fixtures. Expectations are specified independently before evaluating candidate; metadata alone cannot substitute.
rows.coverage: Producer original runtime is explicitly covered in addition to four downstream application installations; original checks can be reused when actual candidate and same contracts are observed.

rows.observation_boundary: Selected installed SDK check invocation using an explicit nonempty compatibility operation document with current consumer parameter/cwd/env/interpreter bindings and its declared application-owned diagnostic. Current prepared profile owner resolves the actual active config and interpreter names; no copy of historical 3.1.0 assumptions. Execute actual selected SDK and real diagnostic; call interpreter path through installed consumer context.
rows.required_behavior: Supported application diagnostic executes through configured command preparation, real child execution and the consumer result interpreter; complete exit/stdout/stderr/interpretation visible.
rows.expected_result: Each required command completes with its owner-declared accepted exit code and expected application diagnostic outcome; SDK reports successful nonempty attempted commands with matching interpreted result. The same context must also correctly reject a deliberately unsatisfied diagnostic result at the interpreter boundary; accepted/rejected cases use independent owner fixtures, not candidate-generated expectations.
rows.oracle: Independent original application diagnostic declaration and consumer-owned supported CLI contract, plus a valid captured pre-update result in the same supported context. Preserve meaningful output/exit/schema and interpreter success/error semantics; normalize only explicitly identified volatile fields. Accepted error/success expectations are fixed before candidate execution. Existing pre-update failures require supported fixture/context arrangement; they are not copied into a successful expected result.

coverage_rule: Refresh current registry/owner bindings at delivery. Classify producer runtime, four application installations and deployment-free test registration as already designed; relate every in-scope independent installation to exactly applicable nonempty behavioral evidence and separate adoption metadata. Test-only excluded registration retains its explicit source classification; new/changed registrations are reclassified before supply completion. A valid version-only observation or empty check cannot satisfy a behavioral row.
counterexample_rejection: Correct version/origin/digest/lock with broken consumer config, interpreter import/meaning or application entry yields failed/missing behavioral outcome in its row, so PKG-R07 and delivery remain unsatisfied. Successful producer observations cannot close another independent consumer row.
independent_expectation_rule: Use consumer-owned pre-change contract/declarations and independently authored expected supported results (or valid reusable pre-update evidence for same supported context). No oracle from new shared implementation, metadata, candidate-produced snapshots, or historical 3.1.0 exact-version assertions. Unknown/unavailable operation context is an uncovered obligation, not compatibility success.
execution_status: Design intentions only. No test creation/execution, deployment or product change.
